subject: Recap + POC monitoring plan: success criteria, dashboards, owners
body:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@techfin.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 15:02:00 -0400
Subject: Recap + POC monitoring plan: success criteria, dashboards, owners

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the proposed POC monitoring / evaluation plan so we can align on next steps and owners. Please skim and confirm (or flag changes) — I want to lock timelines by end of week so we can schedule reserved capacity.

1) POC goals & success criteria (what TechFin told us):
- End-to-end latency: 95th <= 220ms for typical 512-token prompts
- Cost target: <= 0.9x of current baseline per inference for the same throughput profile
- Quality: classification/intent accuracy within 2% of their current on-prem model on the provided eval set
- Reliability: sustained throughput of 60 req/s for 90 minutes without error spikes

2) Observability scope (what we propose we’ll deliver for the POC):
- Pre-built dashboards: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token throughput, GPU utilization, batch sizes
- Tracing: distributed traces for request path (app -> API -> model shard), sample retention and flamegraph for the 95th percentile path
- Logs: structured logs exported to TechFin’s ELK (we’ll provide a Fluent-bit configuration + sample mapping). Redactions applied to PIIs by default.
- Metrics to monitor: request_count, request_latency_ms_{p50,p95,p99}, model_error_count, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_avg, gpu_mem_usage_mb, token_generation_rate

3) Deliverables and owners
- Monitoring templates (Redwood): Hannah (owner) — deliver Grafana dashboard JSON + Prometheus rules by EOD Thu 8/13
- Instrumentation + tracing config (SE): Marcus (owner) — provide Jaeger config and sampling strategy by Mon 8/16
- Log export mapping & retention plan (TechFin + Redwood): Samantha / Daniel + Stephanie — finalize by Tue 8/17
- POC run and validation (joint): Redwood infra + TechFin ML infra — 8/24–8/27 internal test, production-like run 8/31–9/03

4) Evaluation plan and checkpoints
- Week 1 (8/17–8/21): integration, data plumbing, baseline run. Checkpoint: basic metrics flowing to dashboards.
- Week 2 (8/24–8/28): load tests, latency tuning. Checkpoint: hit target throughput with acceptable p95 latency.
- Final validation (8/31–9/03): quality evals against provided eval set + cost reporting. Checkpoint: final sign-off meeting 9/07.

5) Ask from TechFin (what we need to proceed)
- Access: an account-level read/write API key for Redwood to hit the staging cluster, and an ELK ingestion endpoint for logs.
- Eval data: canonical eval set + a small holdout (CSV) for final quality validation.
- A primary technical contact for day-to-day: who should we loop in?

Attachments: I’ve included a short spreadsheet with suggested success criteria thresholds and a rough dashboard sketch to speed alignment.

Next steps: if that looks good, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Marcus and Stephanie (SE + instrumentation) and your infra folks for Wed 8/12 or Thu 8/13.

Thanks —
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

-----Original Message-----
From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@techfin.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@techfin.ai>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:10:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap + POC monitoring plan: success criteria, dashboards, owners

Thanks Hannah — this is great and aligns with what we discussed. A couple of clarifications:

- Latency: the 220ms p95 is for the online scoring path only (not batch re-scoring). Can you confirm the dashboards separate those paths?
- Cost: can you show a simple per-request cost model in the final report (tokens + GPU time)? We’ll need that for procurement.
- Logs: retention for the POC can be 7 days in TechFin ELK if Redwood keeps a rolling 30-day cache on your side.

Primary contact for infra will be Daniel Park (cc’d). We can give an API key scoped to staging; Daniel will send that once we sign the minimal POC NDA (I’ve looped legal internally).

One more ask: do you have a short playbook for tracing sampling? We need guardrails so we don’t exceed our observability quota.

—Sam
Samantha Cole
Sr. ML Platform Engineer | TechFin AI
samantha.cole@techfin.ai | +1 (617) 555-0246

On Tue, Aug 11, 2026 at 16:35 Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Sam / Daniel —
>
> Quick answers inline: we’ll separate online vs batch in the dashboard (different labels). Per-request cost model: yes — we’ll include an exported CSV and a one-slide breakdown for procurement.
>
> For tracing sampling, Marcus will propose a conservative strategy (dynamic sampling tied to error rate + headroom) — see his note below.
>
> I’ve also attached the success-criteria spreadsheet (small) and a dashboard sketch.
>
> Hannah

>
> Quick internal note and proposed sampling + dashboard components (forwarding to keep thread in one place).
>
> - Tracing sampling: start at 1% steady-state, auto-increase to 5% for requests with latency > p95 or that generate an error. Spike protection: if spans/sec > 500, cap sampling and toggle to error-only.
> - Dashboard panels I’ll build: 1) Traffic & error heatmap (by route), 2) Latency distribution w/ flaky outlier table, 3) Model shard utilization, 4) KV cache hit-rate trends, 5) Per-request cost estimate (tokens + GPU ms).
> - Data retention: logs -> ELK (7d), metrics -> Prometheus (30d), traces -> Jaeger (14d). We’ll hand off config snippets for each.
>
> Internal owners: Marcus (tracing + dashboards), Stephanie (log mappings), Hannah (POC owner / customer-facing).
>
> I’ll draft the dashboard JSON and a short runbook for the load-test scenarios (target traj: 60 req/s sustained). Expect first draft by Mon 8/16.
>
> -Marcus
